strategic_priorities: Pacific Islands influence competition with China
vulnerabilities: Extremely long, thinly populated coastline and maritime approaches make comprehensive surveillance and denial of the full northern approaches to Australia a persistent structural challenge
Heavy trade dependence on China as the largest export market (iron ore, coal, LNG), creating economic exposure whenever bilateral political relations sour
Small population base relative to landmass limits the scale of standing military manpower without heavy reliance on technology and alliance backing
AUKUS submarine transition creates a capability gap — the Collins-class fleet must be extended in service until Virginia-class/SSN-AUKUS boats arrive in the 2030s
strengths: Southern Hemisphere anchor of the US alliance system — AUKUS Pillar 1 nuclear-powered submarine partnership and Pine Gap joint intelligence facility
Massive net exporter of energy and minerals (iron ore, LNG, coal, lithium), giving genuine leverage over China's raw-material supply chains despite the trade dependence risk
Stable Western-aligned democratic institutions and deep Five Eyes intelligence integration
Geographic position astride the southern approaches to the Indo-Pacific, relevant to any contingency involving the Malacca/Sunda/Lombok strait system
